exposure: Interpregnancy interval (IPI) categorized as ≤ 11, 12-17, 18-23 (reference), 24-35, 36-59, and ≥ 60 months
outcome: Maternal adverse events (maternal transfusion, ruptured uterus, unplanned hysterectomy, and admission to an intensive care unit)
Neonatal adverse events (low birthweight, premature birth, Apgar score at 5 min < 7, and abnormal conditions of the newborn)
cohort: 792,094 women aged ≥ 18 years with two consecutive singleton pregnancies, whose first delivery was by cesarean delivery
finding: Both short and long IPI were associated with increased risk of repeat cesarean delivery and neonatal adverse events, while a longer IPI may reduce maternal adverse events in women < 35 years.
